metadata.title: Elastic BB knots are multifold circles
metadata.abstract: We study elastic knots obtained by minimizing the bending energy of a unit loop together with a small multiple of ropelength. We assume a generalized Fáry-Milnor inequality on the $C^1$-boundary of a knot class: every $H^2$-limit curve in the $C^1$-closure has total curvature at least $2\pi$ times the bridge index. Under this assumption we prove that every elastic knot in a one-component BB knot class, that is, a class whose bridge and braid indices coincide, is the round circle covered precisely that many times. The proof does not differentiate the nonsmooth ropelength functional. A minimal closed braid is contracted in the fibres of a solid torus, producing a family of comparison curves with quadratic bending-energy excess and thickness of linear order. This yields a lower thickness bound for the regularized minimizers. Variations on an intermediate scale then give free stationarity of the limiting curve for the normalized bending energy. Constant curvature and free stationarity reduce the classification to a linear distributional ordinary differential equation.
